scope: a tenant challenging a rent increase, including nullity for defect of form

requests.why: To verify the form compliance (Art. 269d OR, vmwg Art. 19) and determine the exact receipt date for the 30-day challenge deadline (Art. 270b OR).
To establish the precise date the rent increase notice was received, which is critical for calculating the 30-day contestation period (Art. 270b OR, ZPO Art. 142).
To verify which reference interest rate was applied in the calculation and whether it complies with vmwg Art. 12a requirements.
To assess whether the rent increase is justified by cost increases (Art. 269a OR, vmwg Art. 12) and verify the calculation basis.

scope: a tenant challenging a rent increase, including nullity for defect of form

requests.why: To establish the exact date the rent increase notification was received, which is critical since the 30-day challenge deadline (Art. 270b OR) has apparently passed and the tenant needs to confirm whether the deadline has truly expired.
The tenant explicitly states uncertainty about which reference interest rate was applied; this document is necessary to verify whether the rent increase calculation complied with Art. 12a VMWG.
To compare the previous rent amount with the new amount stated in the increase notification and verify the calculation basis.
If the landlord justified the increase by cost increases (Art. 269a(b) OR), the supporting documentation is needed to assess whether the claimed increases are legitimate under Art. 12 VMWG.

To compare the previous rent amount and any prior increases with the current notification to assess whether the calculation is plausible.

To compare the previous rent with the new rent and verify the calculation accuracy.

scope: a tenant challenging a rent increase, including nullity for defect of form

requests.why: To verify whether the rent increase was properly notified using the required cantonal form (Art. 269d OR) and to assess the stated grounds for the increase.
To establish the exact receipt date of the rent increase notice, which determines the 30-day deadline for contesting it (Art. 270b OR).
To verify the reference mortgage rate applicable at the time of the increase notification, as this is the baseline for assessing whether a rate-based increase is justified (Art. 12a VMWG).
If the landlord cited cost increases as justification, documentation of these costs is needed to assess whether the increase amount is proportionate (Art. 269a(b) OR, Art. 12 VMWG).
To assess whether the new rent falls within local market rates, which is a key criterion for determining if the increase is abusive (Art. 269a(a) OR, Art. 11 VMWG).

scope: a tenant challenging a rent increase, including nullity for defect of form

requests.why: To verify the form complies with Art. 269d OR requirements and to establish the exact receipt date, which determines the 30-day challenge deadline under Art. 270b OR.
To establish the precise date the rent increase was received, as this triggers the 30-day contestation period and the tenant states the exact receipt time remains unresolved.
To verify the prior rent amount and payment history, necessary to assess whether the increase calculation is correct.
To check the reference rate baseline cited in the increase notice, as the tenant specifically identifies this as unresolved and it is central to validating cost-based increases under Art. 12a VMWG.
To verify the landlord's claimed justification for the increase (cost increases or improvements) and assess whether supporting documentation meets Art. 20 VMWG requirements.

scope: a tenant challenging a rent increase, including nullity for defect of form

requests.why: To verify the form date, signature date, and reference rate cited in the rent increase notice, which the tenant reports contains a chronologically inconsistent rate entry (rate dated two weeks after signature).
To establish which official reference rate was applicable on the notice preparation date and verify whether the rate cited in the form matches the correct publication period under VMWG Art. 12a.
To confirm the actual delivery date of the rent increase notice and establish the timeline for the tenant's 30-day challenge period under OR Art. 270b.

To assess whether the rent increase is justified under Art. 269a OR and to enable the tenant to verify the landlord's claimed cost basis if challenging the increase.

To verify which reference rate was actually applicable on the form date and whether the rate cited complies with Art. 12a VMWG's quarterly publication schedule.
To establish the actual delivery date of the rent increase notice, which determines the 30-day challenge deadline under Art. 270b OR that the tenant may have already missed.

scope: a tenant challenging a rent increase, including nullity for defect of form

requests.why: The tenant received a rent increase notice on 31 March 2025 and needs the official form and any accompanying correspondence to verify whether the correct canton-approved form was used and whether the reference rate date, publication period, and calculation basis are properly documented.

The tenant disputes the reference interest rate used in the rent increase calculation due to a temporal discrepancy between the form date and the rate publication date, requiring the official quarterly reference rate publication to verify which rate should have been applied.
To verify the landlord's justification for the rent increase and confirm whether cost increases or other grounds cited comply with legal requirements under Art. 269a OR and VMWG Art. 12.

scope: a tenant challenging a rent increase, including nullity for defect of form

requests.why: The tenant received a rent increase notice on 1 December 2024 and questions the reference rate calculation and form preparation date; the official form and any accompanying correspondence are essential to verify compliance with Art. 269d OR and Art. 19 VMWG regarding proper notification, justification, and reference rate accuracy.

The tenant disputes the reference rate cited in the rent increase notice, claiming a temporal discrepancy between the form date and the rate publication date; the official reference rate publication is necessary to verify whether the correct rate was applied under Art. 12a VMWG.
Payment records establish the tenant's compliance history and current rent amount, which are foundational for evaluating any rent increase challenge under Art. 269–270b OR.

requests.why: To establish a complete chronology of rent payments and verify whether the earlier rent increase was actually implemented.
To document the previous rent increase notification from autumn and compare it with the current increase to identify potential double-counting of the reference rate.
To verify which reference rate periods were applied to each rent increase and determine if the same rate factor was used twice.
To clarify which net rent amount serves as the baseline for calculating increases and to reconcile discrepancies between standing orders and annual statements.

scope: a tenant challenging a rent increase, including nullity for defect of form

requests.why: To establish the exact dates and amounts of all rent increase notifications and verify whether a previous increase was actually implemented.
To create a complete chronology of actual payments versus amounts due and identify any double-counting of the reference rate.
To verify which reference rate periods were applied to each increase notification and detect potential overlapping application of the same rate.
To establish the correct base net rent amount from which each increase was calculated.
To confirm the exact dates when rent increase notifications were received, which determines the 30-day challenge deadline.

scope: a tenant challenging a rent increase, including nullity for defect of form

requests.why: The tenant received a rent increase notice on 20 August 2025 but needs the official form and any accompanying correspondence to verify whether it complies with Art. 269d OR (proper form, reasoning, no termination threat) and to assess the claimed grounds.

To establish a complete chronology of actual payments versus invoiced amounts and to clarify whether a previous rent increase from autumn was actually implemented, as the tenant notes discrepancies between standing orders and annual statements.
To verify the reference interest rate applicable to the claimed increase and determine whether the same rate factor may have been applied twice, as the tenant suspects.
To establish the correct base net rent (Nettomietzins) as the starting point for calculating the increase and to verify whether an earlier increase was actually implemented.
To confirm proper service of the rent increase notice and verify the exact date of receipt, which determines the 30-day challenge deadline under Art. 270b OR.

requests.why: To verify whether a prior rent increase was actually implemented and to establish the correct chronology of all rent increase notifications.
To reconcile notifications, invoices, and actual payments into a single chronology and determine which net rent serves as the baseline for calculating increases.
To verify whether the same reference interest rate factor was applied twice and to assess the lawfulness of the rent increase under Art. 269d OR and VMWG Art. 12a.
To confirm the exact date the rent increase notification was received and verify compliance with formal requirements under Art. 266l OR and VMWG Art. 19.

scope: a tenant challenging a rent increase, including nullity for defect of form

requests.why: To establish whether a rent increase was actually notified and implemented in autumn 2024, and to verify the reference rate used then.
To create a chronology of actual payments versus invoiced amounts and identify any discrepancies or double-charging of the reference rate factor.
To clarify which net rent amount serves as the baseline for calculating the current increase and to verify consistency with payment records.
To verify the reference rate cited in the current increase notice and compare it with any rate used in the autumn 2024 increase to detect potential double application.

scope: a tenant challenging a rent increase, including nullity for defect of form

requests.why: To verify whether the rent increase was properly notified using the required cantonal form and to establish the exact date of notification for the 30-day challenge deadline.
To reconcile the claimed rent payments with actual transactions and determine which net base rent applies as the starting value for the increase calculation.
To verify the reference interest rate applied and confirm whether the same rate factor was potentially applied twice in the autumn increase and current increase.
To establish the rent amount before the autumn increase and clarify whether that earlier increase was actually implemented or only notified.
To confirm the exact date the rent increase notification was received, which determines whether the 30-day challenge period under Art. 270b OR has expired.

requests.why: To establish the chronology of rent increase notifications and verify whether the previous autumn increase was actually implemented or cancelled due to the claimed system error.
To reconcile actual payments against invoiced amounts and determine which net base rent applies as the starting point for calculating increases.
To verify the reference interest rates cited in both the previous and current increase notifications and assess whether the same rate factor was applied twice.
To confirm the exact dates when rent increase notifications were delivered, which determines the 30-day challenge period under Art. 270b OR.

requests.why: The tenant needs to verify whether the rent increase was properly notified using the required cantonal form and to establish the exact date of notification for the 30-day challenge period.
To create the chronology the tenant seeks by comparing actual payments against invoices and to determine which net rent served as the baseline for each increase.
To verify whether the same reference interest rate was applied twice and to assess whether the increase complies with the legal requirements under VMWG Art. 12a.
To establish the correct baseline net rent and clarify which prior increase was allegedly not implemented due to the system error.
To obtain the landlord's official account of the system error, the dates involved, and confirmation of which increases were or were not actually charged.

requests.why: The tenant needs the official rent increase notification form (Art. 269d OR, vmwg Art. 19) to verify whether it contains the required detailed breakdown of costs by category and the legal information about contestation rights; the landlord's correspondence should clarify which subsidies apply.

To determine which portion of facade renovation costs qualifies as value-adding improvements (vmwg Art. 14) versus maintenance, and to verify that work has been completed and supporting documentation exists before any rent increase takes effect.

To obtain itemized documentation of all renovation costs claimed by the landlord, which is necessary to assess whether the proposed rent increase complies with the permissible rate for value-adding investments and to identify applicable subsidies to be deducted (vmwg Art. 14 Abs. 3bis).
To confirm proper service of the rent increase notification and establish the start date of the 30-day contestation period (Art. 270b OR, ZPO Art. 142).

scope: a tenant challenging a rent increase, including nullity for defect of form

requests.why: The tenant received a rent increase notice on 30.04.2025 with only a total amount and no clear breakdown; the official form and any accompanying correspondence are essential to verify compliance with Art. 269d OR and VMWG Art. 19 requirements for proper justification.

To determine which portion of facade renovation costs qualifies as value-adding improvements under VMWG Art. 14, the landlord's detailed cost breakdown and documentation of work performed is required.

To assess whether the rent increase is justified by cost increases under Art. 269a(b) OR and VMWG Art. 12, documentation of specific cost increases (hypothecary interest, insurance, maintenance) must be obtained from the landlord.
To verify what subsidies or grants were received for the renovation work, as VMWG Art. 14(3bis) requires deduction of promotional contributions from the investment costs.
To challenge whether the increased rent falls within customary local rents under Art. 269a(a) OR and VMWG Art. 11, evidence of comparable properties in the same location is needed.
To confirm proper service of the rent increase notice and establish the exact date the 30-day challenge period began under Art. 270b OR and ZPO Art. 142.

scope: a tenant challenging a rent increase, including nullity for defect of form

requests.why: The tenant needs the official rent increase notification form and any accompanying letter to verify whether it complies with Art. 269d OR (required form, clear breakdown, and proper justification) and to assess the claimed renovation costs.

To determine which costs qualify as value-adding improvements under Art. 14 VMWG and to verify whether subsidies were received that must be deducted from the claimed increase per Art. 14 Abs. 3bis VMWG.
To establish the landlord's actual documented costs for the renovation work and verify the calculation basis for the rent increase claim.
To confirm the exact date the rent increase notification was served, which determines the 30-day deadline for filing a conciliation request under Art. 270b OR.

scope: a tenant challenging a rent increase, including nullity for defect of form

requests.why: The tenant needs the official rent increase notification form and any accompanying letter to verify whether it complies with Art. 269d OR (required form, clear reasoning, individual breakdown of grounds per Art. 19 VMWG) and to assess the claimed renovation costs.

To determine what portion of renovation costs qualifies as value-adding improvements under Art. 14 VMWG (which can justify rent increases) versus maintenance costs, and to verify whether subsidies were received and deducted per Art. 14 Abs. 3bis VMWG.

To document the landlord's claimed cost increases and verify they meet the requirements of Art. 12 VMWG (legitimate cost increases such as mortgage rate changes, taxes, insurance) and whether the reference rate applies per Art. 12a VMWG.
To establish the exact date the rent increase was communicated, which determines the 30-day deadline for filing a challenge with the conciliation authority under Art. 270b OR.

scope: a tenant challenging a rent increase, including nullity for defect of form

requests.why: The tenant received a rent increase letter with only a total and no breakdown; the official form and any accompanying correspondence are essential to verify compliance with Art. 269d OR (required form, clear reasoning, individual amounts for each ground) and to assess whether the increase is justified under Art. 269a OR.

To verify the claimed renovation costs and determine the value-adding share under Art. 14 VMWG, which is necessary to assess whether the rent increase exceeds the permissible amount for wertvermehrende Verbesserungen.
To document any subsidies received for the renovation (Art. 14 Abs. 3bis VMWG requires deduction of subsidies from the claimed costs) and to verify the actual net costs justifying the increase.
To establish the baseline rent before the increase and confirm payment history, which is necessary for any subsequent conciliation or dispute proceedings.

scope: a tenant challenging a rent increase, including nullity for defect of form

requests.why: The tenant received a rent increase notice around 4 February 2025 but reports it lacks proper breakdown and justification; the official form and any accompanying correspondence are essential to verify compliance with Art. 269d OR (required form, reasoning, and timing).

The tenant questions the value-adding share of renovation costs and whether subsidies were properly deducted; Art. 14 VMWG requires detailed cost documentation and proof that subsidies were subtracted from the claimed improvement costs.
To verify proper service of the rent increase notice and confirm the exact date of communication, which determines the 30-day challenge deadline under Art. 270b OR.
To establish the baseline rent before the increase and verify payment history, which is necessary to assess whether the increase is proportionate and to support any subsequent challenge.

scope: a tenant challenging a rent increase, including nullity for defect of form

requests.why: The tenant received a rent increase notice around 18 January 2025 but reports it lacks a clear breakdown and subsidy information; the official form and any accompanying letter are essential to assess whether the landlord complied with Art. 269d OR (required form, reasoning, and proper notification).

To verify the claimed renovation costs and determine what portion qualifies as value-adding improvements under Art. 14 VMWG, which is necessary to assess whether the rent increase is justified and not excessive.
To establish whether the landlord has documented cost increases (financing, maintenance, etc.) that support the claimed increase, as required by Art. 269a OR and Art. 20 VMWG for substantiation.
To determine whether the new rent falls within local market rates under Art. 269a(a) OR and Art. 11 VMWG, which is a key criterion for assessing whether the increase is abusive.
To confirm proper service of the rent increase notice and establish the exact date notification was received, which determines the 30-day deadline for contesting the increase under Art. 270b OR.

Required to assess whether the new rent falls within local market standards if the tenant later challenges the increase as abusive (Art. 269a OR, vmwg Art. 11).

scope: a tenant challenging a rent increase, including nullity for defect of form

requests.why: The tenant received a rent increase notice for facade renovation but reports only a total without breakdown; the official form and any accompanying letter are essential to assess compliance with Art. 269d OR (required form, clear reasoning, itemized grounds) and Art. 19 VMWG (detailed justification requirements).

To verify whether the landlord has provided or can provide the itemized costs for the facade renovation, including the value-adding share and any subsidies received, as required by Art. 14 VMWG for assessing permissible rent increases for improvements.
To establish what cost increases (if any) the landlord claims beyond the renovation investment, and to verify compliance with Art. 12 VMWG regarding permissible cost-based increases.
To confirm the tenant's payment history and the previous rent level before the increase, establishing the baseline for assessing whether the increase is proportionate under Art. 269a OR.
To verify proper service of the rent increase notice and confirm the notification date (tenant became aware 15 September 2025), which determines the 30-day deadline for contesting under Art. 270b OR.

scope: a tenant challenging a rent increase, including nullity for defect of form

requests.why: The tenant needs the official rent increase notification form and any accompanying letter to verify compliance with Art. 269d OR (proper form, reasoning, and timing requirements) and to assess the claimed renovation costs.

The tenant explicitly requests clarity on recoverable costs, value-adding share, and subsidy deductions under Art. 14 VMWG, which requires detailed documentation of renovation expenses and any subsidies received.
To verify whether the rent increase is justified by cost increases under Art. 269a(b) OR and Art. 12 VMWG, and to assess the breakdown claimed in the landlord's letter.
To confirm proper service of the rent increase notification as required by Art. 269d OR and to establish the exact date the 30-day challenge period began under Art. 270b OR.

scope: a tenant challenging a rent increase, including nullity for defect of form

requests.why: The case involves a disputed rent increase with unclear reclassification of ancillary charges into net rent; the official form and any landlord communications explaining the increase are essential to assess its legality under Art. 269d OR.
To verify the prior net rent amount and establish the baseline for evaluating whether the claimed increase is justified and properly documented.

The landlord must provide detailed justification for any cost-based increase; this statement is necessary to verify whether claimed cost increases meet the requirements of Art. 269a OR and VMWG Art. 12.
To assess whether the new rent falls within local market rates under Art. 269a(a) OR and VMWG Art. 11, given the tenant's concern about unexplained increases.
If the increase is tied to mortgage rate changes, the current reference rate under VMWG Art. 12a must be documented to verify compliance with legal limits.

scope: a tenant challenging a rent increase, including nullity for defect of form

requests.why: The case involves a rent increase with unexplained reclassification of ancillary charges into net rent; the official form and any landlord communication are essential to verify compliance with Art. 269d OR and to assess the legitimacy of the charge reclassification.

To establish the prior net rent amount and verify the actual payment history, which is necessary to determine the basis for calculating the increase and to assess whether the claimed increase is proportionate.

The landlord must provide detailed justification for any cost-based increase; this document is critical to evaluate whether the reclassification of ancillary charges into net rent is justified under Art. 269a OR.

If the increase is based on mortgage interest rate changes, the current reference rate must be documented to verify compliance with Art. 12a VMWG and to assess whether the increase is within permissible limits.

To verify whether the resulting net rent falls within local market standards under Art. 269a(a) OR and Art. 11 VMWG, which is essential to challenge any misclassification that inflates the net rent artificially.

scope: a tenant challenging a rent increase, including nullity for defect of form

requests.why: The case involves an unexplained reclassification of ancillary charges into net rent; the official form and any landlord communications explaining this change are essential to assess whether the increase complies with Art. 269d OR requirements and whether it is justified.
The tenant needs clarity on the prior net rent to verify whether the claimed increase from ancillary charges to net rent is accurate and to assess the overall rent adjustment.

The latest ancillary-cost statement is missing; obtaining it is necessary to verify the basis for any reclassification and to determine whether cost increases justify the rent modification under Art. 269a OR.
Payment records will confirm the actual gross and net amounts paid historically, helping to establish the baseline for comparison and verify the tenant's claim about the discrepancy.

scope: a tenant challenging a rent increase, including nullity for defect of form

requests.why: The tenant needs the official rent increase notification form to verify compliance with Art. 269d OR requirements and to establish the exact date the increase was communicated, which is critical for the 30-day challenge deadline under Art. 270b OR.
To clarify which previous net rent was binding and to verify the actual net rent increase amount, as the tenant reports confusion about whether costs were reclassified from ancillary to net rent.

The landlord's notification mentions only 'Kostenanpassung' without detail; a detailed cost increase statement is needed to determine whether the increase is justified under Art. 269a(b) OR and to support the tenant's challenge if the basis is inadequate.
If the rent increase is based on mortgage interest rate changes under Art. 12a VMWG, the official reference rate publication on the increase date is necessary to verify the calculation's legality.

scope: a tenant challenging a rent increase, including nullity for defect of form

requests.why: The tenant received a rent increase notice on approximately 17.11.2025 but the message indicates the official form content is unclear regarding whether amounts constitute net rent or ancillary costs; the original notice and any accompanying correspondence are essential to verify compliance with Art. 269d OR form requirements and to clarify the breakdown.

The tenant explicitly states uncertainty about which previous net rent was binding; a statement showing the rent history before the increase is necessary to determine the baseline for evaluating whether the increase is abusive under Art. 269 OR.

The notice mentions only 'Kostenanpassung' without detail, and the tenant lacks the most recent ancillary cost settlement; a detailed cost increase statement from the landlord is required to assess whether cost increases justify the increase under Art. 269a(b) OR.
Payment records establish the actual rent amounts paid and timing, which are necessary to verify the baseline rent and confirm the 140 CHF net increase claimed by the tenant.

Art. 266l OR requires written notice; proof of proper service (registered mail receipt or envelope) is needed to confirm the notice was validly delivered and to establish the start date of the 30-day challenge period under Art. 270b OR.

scope: a tenant challenging a rent increase, including nullity for defect of form

requests.why: The tenant needs to verify whether the landlord used the mandatory cantonal form for the rent increase notice and whether it contains the required detailed breakdown of costs, completion status, and subsidy information per VMWG Art. 19.

The tenant explicitly requests final invoices and clarification of actual costs; the current estimate is provisional and insufficient under VMWG Art. 14 Abs. 5, which requires completed works and supporting documents before a rent increase can be announced.
To verify proper service of the rent increase notice and confirm the start date of the 30-day contestation period under OR Art. 270b.

scope: a tenant challenging a rent increase, including nullity for defect of form

requests.why: To verify whether the rent increase notice complied with Art. 269d OR (required form, timing, and grounds) and to assess the provisional budget claim before works completion.
To obtain the final invoices and cost documentation required under VMWG Art. 14 Abs. 5, since the tenant correctly notes that only completed works with supporting documents justify increases.
To establish the reference mortgage rate applicable at the time of notice if any cost increase is claimed under VMWG Art. 12a.
To confirm proper service of the rent increase notice, which is a prerequisite for the 30-day challenge period under Art. 270b OR.

scope: a tenant challenging a rent increase, including nullity for defect of form

requests.why: The case involves a rent increase notice with an estimated renovation budget before works completion; the official form and any accompanying correspondence are essential to assess whether the notice complies with formal requirements and to evaluate the provisional cost basis.

The tenant disputes the rent increase based on a provisional budget before works are complete and needs final invoices and project completion details; the landlord's cost documentation is necessary to verify whether the increase is justified and whether final costs differ from estimates.

To substantiate the landlord's claimed cost increases for the renovation, the landlord must provide detailed documentation of the actual or projected costs, which is required under VMWG Art. 20 for the tenant to assess the increase's validity.

The rent increase notice must be properly served; proof of delivery via registered mail or equivalent is necessary to establish whether the notice was validly communicated and to determine the start of the 30-day challenge period.

scope: a tenant challenging a rent increase, including nullity for defect of form

requests.why: The tenant received a rent increase notice on 15 January 2025 but did not challenge it by 14 February 2025, so the 30-day contestation period (Art. 270b OR) has expired; however, the official form and correspondence are needed to verify whether the increase was properly justified and whether final costs/completion dates were disclosed as required.

The tenant disputes that the increase is based on a provisional budget before works are complete and needs the landlord's cost documentation, final invoices, and completion timeline to assess whether the increase complies with Art. 14 VMWG (works must be executed and supporting documents must exist before announcing increases).
If any portion of the rent increase is justified by reference interest rate changes under Art. 12a VMWG, the official quarterly publication is needed to verify the calculation.

scope: a tenant challenging a rent increase, including nullity for defect of form

requests.why: The case involves a rent increase notice; the official form and any accompanying correspondence are essential to verify compliance with Art. 269d OR (proper form, timing, and grounds for the increase).

The tenant disputes that works are incomplete and questions whether a provisional budget justifies the increase; final invoices and completion status are critical to assess whether the increase complies with Art. 14 VMWG (works must be executed and supporting documents must exist).

The landlord must provide detailed numerical justification for the increase; this document is necessary to verify compliance with Art. 20 VMWG (tenant's right to demand zahlenmässig begründet justification).

Proof of proper service of the rent increase notice is required to establish that the notice was validly delivered and that the 30-day challenge period under Art. 270b OR has been correctly calculated.

scope: a tenant challenging a rent increase, including nullity for defect of form

requests.why: The tenant received a rent increase notice but needs the official form (Art. 269d OR, vmwg Art. 19) and any accompanying correspondence to verify proper notification, grounds for increase, and whether it complies with legal requirements before the 30-day challenge deadline.

The tenant disputes whether the increase is based on provisional budgets before work completion and needs detailed documentation of actual renovation costs, completion status, final invoices, and any subsidies to assess whether the increase is justified under Art. 269a OR and vmwg Art. 14.

To verify proper service of the rent increase notice as required by Art. 269d OR and to confirm the exact date the notice was received, which determines the 30-day challenge deadline under Art. 270b OR.

scope: a tenant challenging a rent increase, including nullity for defect of form

requests.why: The tenant needs the official rent increase notice and any accompanying documentation to verify compliance with Art. 269d OR (proper form, timing, and justification requirements) and to establish the exact deadline for contesting the increase.

The tenant explicitly requests clarity on final costs and completion status; Art. 14 VMWG requires that rent increases for renovations can only be announced after works are executed and supporting documents are available, so the provisional budget and final invoices are essential to assess legality.

To verify whether the landlord has properly documented and justified the claimed cost increases under Art. 269a OR and Art. 12 VMWG, and to determine if subsidies have been deducted as required by Art. 14 Abs. 3bis VMWG.
To confirm proper service of the rent increase notice as required by Art. 269d OR and to establish the exact date the 30-day contestation period began under Art. 270b OR.

scope: a tenant challenging a rent increase, including nullity for defect of form

requests.why: The case involves a rent increase notice allegedly based on provisional renovation costs before works completion; the official form and any accompanying correspondence are essential to verify compliance with Art. 269d OR (proper form, reasoning, timing) and Art. 19 VMWG (required content including completion status and cost breakdown).

The tenant disputes the provisional budget basis and needs final invoices and subsidy confirmation; Art. 14 VMWG requires that rent increases for improvements be announced only after works are executed and supporting documents are available, making the cost documentation critical to assess legality.

If any portion of the increase relates to mortgage interest rate changes, the official reference rate at the time of notice is required to verify compliance with Art. 12a VMWG and to assess whether the increase is justified under Art. 269a(b) OR.

The tenant must verify proper service of the rent increase notice to confirm the 30-day challenge deadline under Art. 270b OR has been correctly calculated and that Art. 266n OR (separate service requirements) were met.

To confirm whether the landlord used the required cantonal form for the rent increase notification and whether it complies with VMWG Art. 19 requirements regarding timing and justification.
To obtain the landlord's documentation of project status, completion date of renovation work, and confirmation of when final costs and subsidy decisions were determined.
To verify the exact date the rent increase notification was received, which determines the 30-day contestation deadline under Art. 270b OR.

scope: a tenant challenging a rent increase, including nullity for defect of form

requests.why: To verify the form compliance (Art. 269d OR, vmwg Art. 19) and determine the exact notification date, which is critical for the 30-day challenge deadline (Art. 270b OR).
To establish the precise date the rent increase notification was received, as this triggers the 30-day contestation period under Art. 270b OR.
To verify which reference interest rate was applied to the rent increase calculation, as required under vmwg Art. 12a for mortgage rate adjustments.
To substantiate any claimed cost increases (vmwg Art. 12) and verify whether the landlord provided the required numerical justification (vmwg Art. 20).
To assess whether the increased rent falls within customary local rates (Art. 269a OR, vmwg Art. 11) if the increase is challenged as abusive.

scope: a tenant challenging a rent increase, including nullity for defect of form

requests.why: The case involves an unexplained reclassification of ancillary charges into net rent; the official form and any accompanying landlord correspondence are essential to understand the basis and legality of the claimed increase.
The tenant explicitly states the prior net rent remains unresolved; a previous rent statement is necessary to establish the baseline and verify the claimed increase amount.
The form indicates only 'cost adjustment' as justification; a detailed cost increase statement is needed to verify whether the increase is justified under OR Art. 269a.
Payment records will establish the chronology of rent amounts and dates, clarifying the sequence of changes and helping resolve the timeline uncertainty the tenant mentions.
